DesktopModeNone: No desktop-mode HID device detected. After entering Windows desktop mode, refresh and select the target serial to return.
DesktopModeSelectTarget: Select the display to return to USB display mode.
DesktopModeSwitching: Returning {0} to USB display mode; waiting for its interface…
DesktopModeRestored: {0} USB display interface restored. Studio can send images and video.
DesktopModeNotRestored: Could not restore USB display mode. Check the device connection and refresh.
PacketDirectoryFragment: This is one directory response and may be a blank fragment, not proof of an empty directory. Refresh On-device media under Advanced controls for the full list and check completeness.
PacketBlockFileSize: Select a nonempty file block no larger than 1 MiB.
PacketBlockFileHelp: First create the destination with command 38. This sends one final block, padded to a 1 MiB buffer with its valid length encoded automatically.
PacketSmallFileHelp: The parent directory must exist. Query it with 99 first, then verify the written size with 98. An acknowledgement alone does not prove the file was stored.
PacketDecimalBufferHint: Enter capacity, valid byte count, final flag (0/1), e.g. 1048576 1024 1. Payload fills capacity; valid count cannot exceed it.
PacketDecimalClockHint: Enter year month day hour minute second mode, e.g. 2026 11 19 10 30 0 1. Modes: 0 disable, 1 show, 2 sync only.
PacketDecimalOrientationHint: Enter direction code 0–3 for 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°. The 12.3-inch firmware direction must remain 0.
PacketDecimalBrightnessHint: Enter raw device brightness 0–100, or 0–80 for 12.3-inch. Zero turns off the backlight. This is not a percentage.
PacketDecimalSyncHint: Enter 0 to disable clock synchronization, or 1 to enable it.
Packet0123NativeOrientation: For the 12.3-inch display, enter 0. To rotate the picture, use the orientation control on the Media page.
PacketPngWrittenWithoutReply: PNG command written. This firmware does not acknowledge PNG; check the physical display to confirm output.
PacketDecimalBytesHint: Enter decimal bytes from 0 to 255 in protocol order, separated by spaces. Example: 255 0 128.
PacketDecimalLengthHint: Enter the payload byte count (0–4294967295), e.g. 1024. Encoded as a 4-byte big-endian length.
PacketDecimalBlockHint: Enter block byte count and final-block flag (0 or 1), separated by spaces. Example: 1024 0. Length is encoded as 4-byte big-endian.
PacketPathInputHint: Enter an absolute ASCII device path, e.g. /usr/data/img/test.jpg. Path length and bytes are encoded automatically.
PacketInputInvalid: Check the selected input format, value range and field hints.
PacketEncodingHint: Input is encoded into protocol bytes automatically. Changing format clears that input. No manual path-length calculation is needed.
PlaybackResumeTimedOut: Playback could not resume because the display did not become ready.
DisplayDisconnectedWaitingToResume: Display disconnected. Waiting to resume after reconnection.

BenchmarkStaticImageNotice: The fixed image is pre-encoded. Only USB time is measured.
BenchmarkUsbTime: Average USB send and reply: {0:F1} ms

InvalidSlideshowInterval: Enter a slideshow interval from 0.03 to 3600 seconds.

DeletedFileNotListed: The refreshed directory did not list the file.

DirectoryIncompleteVerifyDeletion: The directory response was incomplete. Refresh the file list to verify deletion.
DeviceDirectoryEmpty: The device returned no files. The folder may be empty or storage may be unavailable.
VerifyFileDeletionFailed: Could not verify deletion. Refresh the file list. {0}

StatusIncludesVoltageHint: Read firmware, storage and supply voltage on demand.
StatusReadHint: Read firmware and storage on demand.
ConnectDisplayHint: Connect a Win207 display to discover it automatically.
SceneLoadedStartOrAddBackground: Scene loaded. Start output or add a video background.

SomeDeviceStatusFieldsAreUnavailable: Some device status fields are unavailable.
EnterProtocolSearch: Enter a command name, ID or keyword.

SelectCommandHint: Select a command to see its purpose and usage.
NoCapturableWindows: No capturable windows. Open and restore the target window.
SelectValidLiveSource: Choose a valid foreground source or video background.
OrientationSaved: Orientation saved. It will be applied when playback starts.
DisplaySettingsPending: Settings saved. Waiting to send them to the display.
DisplaySettingsSendFailed: Settings saved, but the device could not be updated.
ErrorPlaybackStopUnconfirmed: The host stopped sending video, but the display did not confirm that playback stopped. {0}
ErrorCaptureWindowUnavailable: The window is closed, minimized or unresponsive. Restore it and try again.
ErrorCaptureWindowTooLarge: The window is outside the supported capture size.
ErrorCreateCaptureSurface: Could not create the window capture surface.
ErrorAllocateCaptureSurface: Could not allocate the window capture surface.
ErrorWindowFrameUnavailable: This window did not provide a frame.
SetAndShowTheFirmwareClock: Set and show the firmware clock
ReadOrientationOnTheEncryptedChannel: Read orientation on the encrypted channel
DesktopModeRestartRequired: Desktop mode was acknowledged. Send command 11 (Restart device) separately to apply it.
ErrorUseCommandFeaturePage: Use the corresponding feature page to send this command.
CouldNotOpenDocumentationLink: Could not open the documentation link. Check your default browser settings in Windows.
H264BlockSizeDetails: H.264 block size: {0} bytes (0 uses the default)
BrightnessArgumentsHint: Brightness (1 byte). For example, 32 = 50. Range 00–64; the 12.3-inch display uses 0–80 in decimal.
FrameRateArgumentsHint: Playback rate (1 byte). For example, 1E = 30 FPS. Range 01–3C.
DevicePathArgumentsHint: 4-byte big-endian path length + 00 00 00 00 + ASCII path bytes.
FileBufferArgumentsHint: Enter 4-byte big-endian buffer capacity, 4-byte big-endian valid length, then the last-block flag (00 / 01).
DeviceFileArgumentsHint: 4-byte big-endian path length + 4-byte big-endian file length + ASCII path bytes.
VideoClockSyncArgumentsHint: Video clock sync (1 byte). 00 disables it, 01 enables it.
DeviceClockArgumentsHint: Enter year (2 bytes, big-endian), month, day, hour, minute, second, then mode (00 off / 01 on / 02 set time only).
ImageLengthArgumentsHint: Enter the image length (4 bytes, big-endian). For example, 00 00 04 00 = 1024 bytes.
PacketVideoSelected: H.264 configured as the media background. You remain on the Commands page. Switch to Media to play the whole stream; for video only, clear the foreground and start playback.
PacketInvalidDevicePath: Enter an absolute ASCII file path on the device.
PacketShortFileSize: Command 40 requires a nonempty file smaller than 100 KiB.
PacketImageSize: The image must be nonempty and at most 950,000 bytes.
PacketInvalidPng: Use a complete 8-bit RGBA PNG with an alpha channel.
StartupConfigurationArgumentsHint: Enter 7 bytes in order. Decimal ranges are brightness 0–100, startup mode 0–2, fixed 0, orientation 0–3, fixed 0, offline mode 0–1, and fixed 0.
PumpAndFanArgumentsHint: 16 bytes. The first three are FF 0F A1, bytes 5–6 hold the big-endian pump value, and bytes 7–9 hold three fan values.
LedPixelPayloadHint: LED start index + two padding bytes + RGB data. For example, the first block starts with 00 00 00.
CoolingSpeedArgumentsHint: Pump and fan targets, 2 big-endian bytes each. For example, 06 D6 06 D6 sets both to 1750.
FileBufferPayloadHint: Enter the full buffer as hex bytes. The header specifies the valid length.
DeviceFilePayloadHint: Enter the file contents as hex bytes. The length must match the header.
JpegPayloadHint: Enter the complete JPEG as hex bytes, typically starting with FF D8 FF.
PngPayloadHint: Enter the complete PNG as hex bytes, starting with 89 50 4E 47.
H264PayloadHint: Enter the H.264 Annex B block as hex bytes.
RgbAnimationPayloadHint: 2-byte big-endian frame count + 1-byte frame interval + animation data.
HexArgumentsHint: Enter the command arguments as hex, two digits per byte, for example 00 01.
HexPayloadHint: Enter the command payload as hex, two digits per byte, for example 00 FF.
UnknownArgumentsHint: Enter header arguments from the model’s protocol specification using two hexadecimal digits per byte.
UnknownPayloadHint: Enter the payload from the model’s protocol specification using two hexadecimal digits per byte.
NoDecodedResponse: No decoded result is available for this command. See the raw device response.
NoDescriptionIsAvailableForThisCommand: No description is available for this command.
PacketArgumentsHelp: Arguments start at offset 8 in the encrypted header or offset 1 in a raw packet. Hex bytes may be space-separated.
IncompleteHexByte: Enter complete pairs of hexadecimal digits.
InvalidRawPacketLength: The raw channel accepts up to 63 argument bytes and no separate payload.
EncryptedArgumentsTooLong: The encrypted header accepts up to 492 argument bytes.
SceneLoadedSelectTargetDisplay: Scene loaded. Select a target display.
ErrorStoredCommandKeyInvalid: Studio could not read or use the saved command key. If the file is in use, release it and try again. Otherwise, set WINUSB_DISPLAY_COMMAND_KEY and restart.
ErrorCommandKeyUnusable: WINUSB_DISPLAY_COMMAND_KEY is invalid. Check the 16 hexadecimal characters supplied with the firmware.
ErrorDeviceReturnedNoData: The display did not return data. Try again.
ErrorUnexpectedDeviceReply: No reply matched the requested command.
ErrorDeviceDirectoryCreationFailed: The display could not create the requested directory.
ErrorDeviceDisconnected: The device disconnected or its interface is unavailable.
ErrorDisplayInUse: The display is in use. Stop output in the other application and try again.
ErrorDisplayAccessDenied: Windows denied access to the display. Check the WinUSB driver and device permissions.
ErrorIoOperation: A file or device I/O operation failed.
ErrorRequiredFileMissing: A required file could not be found.
WaitingForTheSelectedDisplayToReconnect: Waiting for the selected display to reconnect.
ErrorUsbWriteTimeout: The USB write timed out. Unplug and reconnect this display's USB cable, then try again.
FfmpegConfigured: FFmpeg is configured. You can send the video again.
ErrorFfmpegNotFound: FFmpeg was not found. Select ffmpeg.exe using the FFmpeg button on the Media page and try again.
ErrorWindowCaptureTimedOut: Window capture timed out. Restore the target window and try again.
CommandDetail.GET_FIRMWARE_VERSION: Read the selected display’s firmware version. Open Parsed result to view the version number.
CommandDetail.RESTART_DEVICE: Restart the selected display. It briefly disconnects and can be used again when it reappears.
CommandDetail.SHUT_DOWN_DEVICE: Shut down the selected display on models that support this operation.
CommandDetail.SET_DISPLAY_ORIENTATION: Set the display orientation. For everyday rotation, use the orientation control on the Media page.
CommandDetail.SET_DISPLAY_BRIGHTNESS: Adjust the backlight. Enter a device brightness value, or enter 0 to turn the backlight off.
CommandDetail.SET_VIDEO_FRAME_RATE: Set the display’s video playback rate. Enter the number of frames per second.
CommandDetail.GET_H264_BLOCK_SIZE: Read the display’s preferred H.264 block size for streaming video in blocks.
CommandDetail.CREATE_DEVICE_FILE: Create a file in display storage. Enter its path on the display, then use Write a file buffer to send its contents.
CommandDetail.WRITE_DEVICE_FILE_BLOCK: Write a block to a file you have created on the display. Browse for a local file to set the length and final-block flag automatically.
CommandDetail.WRITE_DEVICE_FILE: Copy a small local file to display storage. Select the file and enter its destination path on the display.
CommandDetail.DELETE_DEVICE_PATH: Delete a file or directory from display storage. Check the path on the display before sending.
CommandDetail.SET_VIDEO_CLOCK_SYNC: Choose whether video playback on the display uses a synchronized clock.
CommandDetail.GET_SUPPLY_VOLTAGE: Read the display’s supply voltage. Open Parsed result to view the reading.
CommandDetail.SET_DEVICE_CLOCK: Set the display clock. Enter the date, time and mode, or use Advanced controls to sync the computer’s clock.
CommandDetail.GET_ORIENTATION_STATE: Read the current orientation and the sensor orientation reported by the display.
CommandDetail.SET_PUMP_SPEED: Cooling speeds are managed through a dedicated USB controller. This operation is unavailable for the displays listed in Studio.
CommandDetail.GET_PUMP_SPEED: Cooling speeds are managed through a dedicated USB controller. This operation is unavailable for the displays listed in Studio.
CommandDetail.GET_DEVICE_FILE_SIZE: Read the size of a file on the display. Enter its path to view the size in bytes.
CommandDetail.LIST_DEVICE_DIRECTORY: Query an existing directory on the display. For the full list, refresh On-device media in Advanced controls.
CommandDetail.GET_STORAGE_CAPACITY: View total, used and available space for flash storage and the SD card.
CommandDetail.DISPLAY_JPEG: Select a local JPEG image to show on the display. The file size is entered automatically.
CommandDetail.DISPLAY_PNG_OVERLAY: Select a local PNG to overlay on the display. Transparent areas reveal the content beneath.
CommandDetail.START_LOCAL_H264_PLAYBACK: Play an H.264 file already stored on the display. Enter its path on the display.
CommandDetail.STOP_LOCAL_H264_PLAYBACK: Stop playback of a video stored on the display.
CommandDetail.GET_LOCAL_H264_PLAYBACK_ST: Check whether a video stored on the display is currently playing.
CommandDetail.DISPLAY_LOCAL_JPEG: Show a JPEG image already stored on the display. Enter its path on the display.
CommandDetail.STOP_LOCAL_JPEG_LOOP: Stop the slideshow of images stored on the display.
CommandDetail.WRITE_H264_STREAM_BLOCK: Send one block of H.264 video data. To play a complete file, select the H.264 file and start playback on the Media page.
CommandDetail.GET_H264_QUEUE_DEPTH: See how many H.264 blocks are queued for playback on the display.
CommandDetail.STOP_H264_STREAM: Stop the current video stream sent over USB.
CommandDetail.SET_DEVICE_CONFIGURATION: Change the display’s startup settings. Common options are also available in Advanced controls.
CommandDetail.SWITCH_TO_DESKTOP_MODE: Set the display to enter Windows desktop mode on its next startup. After sending this command, send Restart device (11) separately to apply the setting.
CommandDetail.GET_DEVICE_POSITION_INDEX: Read the position index reported by the device. The reply format depends on the model.
CommandDetail.SYNC_PUMP_AND_FAN_OUTPUTS: Set the pump and fan outputs together on a compatible device. Use the values specified for the model.
CommandDetail.WRITE_RGB_ANIMATION: Send RGB lighting animation data to a compatible device.
CommandDetail.WRITE_LED_PIXEL_BLOCK: Set a block of RGB colors starting at the specified LED.
CommandDetail.GET_COOLING_TEMPERATURES: Cooling speeds are managed through a dedicated USB controller. This operation is unavailable for the displays listed in Studio.
CommandDetail.SET_COOLING_SPEEDS: Cooling speeds are managed through a dedicated USB controller. This operation is unavailable for the displays listed in Studio.
CommandDetail.GET_COOLING_SPEEDS: Cooling speeds are managed through a dedicated USB controller. This operation is unavailable for the displays listed in Studio.
PacketDecimalPumpFansHint: Enter the pump value (0–65535) followed by three fan values (0–255), separated by spaces.
PacketDecimalCoolingHint: Enter the pump and fan device values (each 0–65535), separated by a space.
